title: Four regularisers, one shrinkage
brief: Implement inverted dropout, weight decay, label smoothing, and the formula that turns a step count into the ridge penalty it corresponds to.
hints: dropout_forward's mask should not depend on the values in x, only on its shape: draw it as rng.random(x.shape) < (1 - p), so re-seeding rng before two different calls with different x reproduces the same mask.
dropout_backward is the same linear operation as the forward pass applied to the upstream gradient: dx = dout * mask / (1 - p).
label_smoothing_grad is p - y_smooth, where p = softmax(logits) and y_smooth is the smoothed target distribution, divided by the batch size to match a mean-reduced loss.
Building y_smooth as (1 - eps) * one_hot(targets) + eps / K broadcasts cleanly if you build one_hot with np.eye(K)[targets].

early_stopping_equivalent_ridge is gamma = eigenvalue * (1 - step * eigenvalue)**iterations / (1 - (1 - step * eigenvalue)**iterations); guard the case iterations == 0, where the formula's denominator is exactly zero and gamma should be treated as infinite.
For the final check, gradient descent on a diagonal quadratic decouples into one independent 1-D problem per coordinate, so you can call early_stopping_equivalent_ridge once per eigenvalue.
